explanation: There's no single UK-wide rule on shoes indoors - it depends on the household, and the split is more generational than universal. A 2025 survey found 78% of 18-34 year-olds have a 'shoes-off' rule at home, compared with only 51% of those over 55, so younger and more recently-renovated homes increasingly expect shoes off, while others genuinely don't mind. Removing your shoes unprompted is never wrong, but insisting on it when a host waves it off can feel oddly formal.
local_tip: If unsure, ask 'Should I take my shoes off?' when you arrive, or simply follow what the host and other guests do.
regional_note: Shoe removal is somewhat less common in rural homes, partly because cold stone floors and frequent trips between the house and garden make it less practical.

also_check.note: Removing shoes at the entrance is a strict, near-universal rule, and indoor slippers are usually provided.
Most Germans remove shoes on entering a home, and hosts often offer house slippers.
Similarly variable by household and region - common in many homes, especially colder areas, but not universal.
